items.q: A client sends a well-formed request to create an order, but the item is out of stock. Which status code family is correct?
options: 4xx, because the request cannot be fulfilled due to client-side state
5xx, because the server could not complete it
items.explain: The server worked correctly; the problem is with what was asked, so a 4xx like 409 Conflict or 400 fits, not a 5xx.

items.q: Spring Boot: a JSON body should be mapped into an OrderRequest object in a POST handler. Which annotation goes on the parameter?
items.explain: @RequestBody tells Spring to deserialize the request body (JSON) into the object; @RequestParam reads query or form fields.

options: After the handler finishes, for every request
Only when the handler raises an exception
items.explain: A yield dependency runs the code before yield at request start and the code after it (the finally) at request end, so each request gets and releases its own session.

options: 200 with an order for an empty customer
items.explain: With @Valid, a failed bean validation raises MethodArgumentNotValidException, which Spring maps to 400 by default.

items.q: FastAPI: which decorator makes a handler return 201 on a successful POST?
items.explain: status_code on the route sets the default success status; returning 201 from the body would just send the number as JSON.

items.q:
FastAPI test:

client = TestClient(app)
r = client.get("/health")
assert r.status_code == 200
assert r.json() == {"ok": True}

The handler is: return {"ok": "true"}. Which assertion fails?
options: The json assertion, because "true" is a string, not a boolean
Neither, JSON treats them the same
items.explain: The route works (200), but JSON distinguishes the string "true" from the boolean true, so the dict comparison fails.

items.q: Spring Boot: a service method updates two tables and the second update fails. You want the first one rolled back too. What is the simplest fix?
options: Catch the exception and call repo.flush()
items.explain: @Transactional wraps the method in one database transaction that rolls back on a runtime exception.
